story: A synthetic Anchorage local news site published hundreds of AI written stories in 19 days, told readers on each one that no journalist reviewed it, then stopped dead and stayed live

claims.claim: The site dailyanchorage.news carries the tagline "Local News, Anchorage. Every Day."
claims.verbatim: Local News, Anchorage. Every Day.
claims.note: Publisher describing itself, so primary. Page carries no publication date, so date_of_source is the fetch date.

claims.claim: The site states it publishes daily, using the words "Every Day" and "published daily".
claims.verbatim: published daily
claims.note: The hinge of the story. The site claims daily publication and has published nothing since July 26th, 2026. Pair with C05.

claims.claim: The sitemap at dailyanchorage.news lists more than 500 article URLs.
claims.verbatim: https://dailyanchorage.news/article/news-anchorage-20260724-a3d4b867ca7a
claims.note: SOFTENED, NO EXACT NUMBER MAY SHIP. Three counts of the same file returned 1,064 total URLs, 501 article URLs and 1,012 url elements. Only the floor common to every count ships. Slide copy reads "more than 500" and never a precise figure.

claims.claim: The earliest article date in the sitemap is July 8th, 2026.
claims.verbatim: https://dailyanchorage.news/article/policy-anchorage-20260708-c6dd442dccff
claims.note: Two independent fetches agreed. The date is encoded in the article slug itself, which is why this is firmer than the count.

claims.claim: The most recent article on the site is dated July 26th, 2026 and the sitemap lists nothing later.
claims.verbatim: Latest article date: July 26, 2026
claims.note: Corroborated by the sitemap and separately by the homepage. Checked August 13th, 2026, so 18 days without publishing while claiming to publish daily.

claims.claim: Articles on dailyanchorage.news carry a notice saying the article was written by AI and was not reviewed by a journalist before publishing.
claims.verbatim: This article was written by AI from the linked sources and was not reviewed by a journalist before publishing.
claims.note: STRONGEST CLAIM IN THE RUN. Verified verbatim on two different articles, see C07. The deck is built around this sentence.

claims.claim: The identical AI disclosure notice appears on a second, unrelated article on the same site.
claims.verbatim: This article was written by AI from the linked sources and was not reviewed by a journalist before publishing.
claims.note: Two of two articles sampled carried it. Copy says "on the articles we checked" and never "on every article", because the sample is two, not the corpus.

claims.claim: The site's editorial standards page says its articles are produced under human oversight.
claims.verbatim: Our articles are produced with AI-assisted research and drafting under human oversight.
claims.note: The contradiction. The policy page says human oversight, the article page says no journalist reviewed it. Both are the publisher's own words, which is what makes the pairing fair rather than a gotcha.

claims.claim: The editorial standards page says a human editor reviews flagged content, not all content.
claims.verbatim: A human editor reviews flagged content before publication.
claims.note: The nuance that keeps the deck honest. The site never claims every article gets human review, so the two statements reconcile. The deck says the disclosure sits at article level while the masthead language reads as newsroom language. It does NOT say the site lied.

claims.claim: The site labels itself with the badge "Beta, AI-assisted, human oversight".
claims.verbatim: Beta · AI-assisted · human oversight
claims.note: The verbatim uses middot separators. On a slide keep middots or use commas. Never convert them to em or en dashes.

claims.claim: The about page says the site clearly discloses AI involvement on every page.
claims.verbatim: We clearly disclose AI involvement on every page.
claims.note: The site is telling the truth here and the deck must say so. The story is not concealment. It is that a fully disclosed synthetic outlet still stands up as Anchorage local news.

claims.claim: The about page tells readers that details may be imperfect and asks them to verify anything important.
claims.verbatim: Details may be imperfect, so please verify anything important.
claims.note: A local news site asking readers to verify its own reporting. Strong quotable slide line.

claims.claim: Stories on the site are bylined to desks such as "Anchorage Tech Desk" and "Anchorage News Desk" rather than to named reporters.
claims.verbatim: By Anchorage Tech Desk
claims.note: Homepage also showed Anchorage Policy Desk, Anchorage Sport Desk and Anchorage Wellness Desk. No named human reporter was found anywhere on the site.

claims.claim: The site's ownership page names Shane Anderson as founder and names no corporate legal entity.
claims.verbatim: The Daily Anchorage is part of The Daily Network, a group of local news sites that share common ownership. Shane Anderson is the Founder.
claims.note: The page names no registered company, no jurisdiction and no business structure. The fact-checker did NOT independently verify that this person exists or is connected to the site. Attribute as what the page says. USE WITH CARE, a named individual is not this deck's target and the slide-worthy fact is the ABSENCE of a legal entity, not the name.

claims.claim: The site says it is produced centrally by one small team as part of The Daily Network.
claims.verbatim: Part of The Daily Network, a group of local news sites under common ownership and produced centrally by one small team.
claims.note: Confirmed on both the about page and the ownership page.

claims.claim: The parent site dailynetwork.news describes itself as "The Daily World, a daily paper for every city".
claims.verbatim: The Daily World, a daily paper for every city
claims.note: The page also carries the line "The world, city by city".

claims.claim: The parent network page lists 18 city mastheads and every one of them is an Australian city.
claims.verbatim: The Daily Adelaide
claims.note: Two independent fetches returned the same 18 mastheads in the same order, which is why this count survives where the sitemap count did not. Named cities include Adelaide, Brisbane, Melbourne, Perth, Sydney, Darwin and Canberra. Corrects the scout, which said 17.

claims.claim: The Daily Anchorage is not listed among the mastheads on its own parent network page.
claims.verbatim: No United States or Alaska cities appear on this page. All mastheads reference Australian cities only.
claims.note: The verbatim is the fetch tool's reading of the masthead list rather than a printed sentence, because an absence has no quote. The list was returned identically twice. Frame ONLY as "Anchorage does not appear on the network's own list of cities".

claims.claim: The parent network says it is in a hyperscale phase and seeing very high global demand across its sites.
claims.verbatim: We are in a hyperscale phase and seeing very high global demand across our sites.
claims.note: Verified verbatim on two separate fetches. "Hyperscale" is data center vocabulary applied to local news.

claims.claim: An article bylined Anchorage News Desk on the Anchorage site is about a United States House spending vote and names no Alaska person, company or agency.
claims.verbatim: The U.S. House approved a stopgap spending bill on July 21, 2026, by a 220-205 vote, mostly along party lines.
claims.note: Shows local branding sitting on national wire-style content. The 220-205 vote itself was NOT verified against Congress and the deck must not assert it as fact, only as what this site published.

claims.claim: An Anchorage tech article on the site sources a $1.6 billion economic figure to "data cited in coding bootcamp research".
claims.verbatim: according to data cited in coding bootcamp research
claims.note: The attribution names no study, author or year. Present as an example of unfalsifiable sourcing. The deck must NOT repeat the $1.6 billion as true.

claims.claim: The same synthetic article names the Dena'ina Convention Center, a real Anchorage venue, and two real downtown addresses, 721 W 1st Ave and 911 W 8th Ave, alongside its unverifiable figures.
claims.verbatim: Dena'ina Convention Center
claims.note: The honest complication and the deck is better for including it. The content is not pure invention. It braids real Anchorage referents with figures that cannot be checked, which is what makes it hard to dismiss at a glance. The article also names the addresses 721 W 1st Ave and 911 W 8th Ave.

claims.claim: The site maintains full local news section pages including politics, property, schools, transport and things to do.
claims.verbatim: https://dailyanchorage.news/politics
claims.note: The two sitemap reads disagreed on how many non-article pages exist, 24 versus 12, so NO count ships on this. The named sections were listed identically. Corrections and legal-notices pages are also present, the furniture of a real local paper.

claims.claim: Alaska's 2026 primary election is August 18th and it is a top four primary.
claims.verbatim: The August 18 election is a Top Four Primary. Ranked Choice voting is for November 3 General Election.
claims.note: Primary source, the state election authority. This deck runs five days before that election. Use for TIMING only. There is NO evidence linking the synthetic site to the election and the deck must not imply one.

claims.claim: Public Citizen's election deepfake legislation tracker does not list Alaska as having enacted a law.
claims.verbatim: Last updated: August 3, 2026
claims.note: Tracker last updated August 3rd, 2026, inside the window. Secondary source, an advocacy organisation's tracker, so any on-slide use must read "according to Public Citizen's tracker". Confirmed on two separate fetches.

claims.claim: Public Citizen's tracker records that Alaska SB 64 passed the Senate in May 2025 and passed the House in 2026 with the election deepfake provision removed.
claims.verbatim: Introduced Jan. 2025, Passed Senate May 2025, Passed House 2026, Election deepfake provision removed
claims.note: Single sourced. akleg.gov and LegiScan both return 403, so this could NOT be independently confirmed. Must be attributed in the words "according to Public Citizen's tracker" and must never be stated as established legislative fact.

claims.claim: Public Citizen's tracker records Alaska SB 2 as introduced in January 2025 and failed in May 2026.
claims.verbatim: Introduced Jan. 2025, Failed May 2026
claims.note: Say "failed in May 2026" and no more precise than that. The sine die date, the sponsor and the bill's label wording were all DROPPED as unverifiable.

claims.claim: Public Citizen's tracker lists more than 20 states as having enacted laws on deepfakes in elections.
claims.verbatim: Last updated: August 3, 2026
claims.note: SOFTENED. Two reads of the same tracker returned 33 and then 23 enacted states. NCSL 403, Ballotpedia empty. Only the common floor ships, as "more than 20 states, according to Public Citizen's tracker as of August 3rd, 2026". The op-ed's "roughly 30" must NOT be repeated.

claims.claim: The Alaska House passed House Bill 47 carrying criminal penalties for AI generated sexual content and synthetic child sexual abuse material.
claims.verbatim: House passes bill with criminal penalties for AI-generated sexual content, synthetic child sexual abuse material, malicious deepfakes
claims.note: BACKGROUND, outside the window, single sourced to an openly partisan outlet, headline only. Proves HOUSE PASSAGE ONLY. Enactment could NOT be confirmed. If used, copy says the House passed it and never that Alaska enacted it.

claims.claim: The University of Alaska Fairbanks was awarded a $499,000,000 indefinite delivery indefinite quantity contract announced on August 7th, 2026.
claims.verbatim: University of Alaska Fairbanks, Fairbanks, Alaska, was awarded a $499,000,000 cost-no-fee, cost-plus-fixed-fee, firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract
claims.note: Primary federal source, quoted verbatim, inside the window. Solid on the money. Not this deck's story, see C36.

claims.claim: The contract is for scientific and engineering capabilities focused on the geophysical detection of nuclear proliferation as part of an approved University Affiliated Research Center.
claims.verbatim: for essential scientific and engineering capabilities focused on the geophysical detection of nuclear proliferation as part of an approved University Affiliated Research Center
claims.note: Verbatim from the announcement.

claims.claim: The contract number is W911NF-26-D-A013 and the contracting activity is Army Contracting Command at Aberdeen Proving Ground, Maryland.
claims.verbatim: Army Contracting Command, Aberdeen Proving Ground, Maryland, is the contracting activity (W911NF-26-D-A013).
claims.note: Confirms the scout's contract number exactly.

claims.claim: The contract has an estimated completion date of August 6th, 2031.
claims.verbatim: Work locations and funding will be determined with each order, with an estimated completion date of Aug. 6, 2031.
claims.note: Five years and one day from the announcement, internally consistent.

claims.claim: One bid was solicited and one was received for the UAF contract.
claims.verbatim: One bid was solicited with one received.
claims.note: Sole source in effect. Normal for a designated UARC, so it is NOT a procurement irregularity and must not be framed as one.

claims.claim: The August 7th, 2026 contract announcement does not contain the words artificial intelligence, machine learning, algorithm or data science.
claims.verbatim: The terms "artificial intelligence," "machine learning," "AI," "algorithm," and "data science" do not appear anywhere on this page.
claims.note: DECISIVE NEGATIVE, a verified absence on a primary document.

claims.claim: No fetched source connects the UAF nuclear proliferation detection contract to artificial intelligence or machine learning.
claims.verbatim: no stories matching any of your specified criteria
claims.note: STOP SIGN FOR CANDIDATE B. war.gov carries no AI language, UAF's newsroom carries no story on this contract, uarc.gi.alaska.edu returned 503 twice. The AI framing is UNVERIFIED and this contract must NOT anchor an AI deck.

claims.claim: The Department of the Air Force will hold a microreactor project town hall on August 26th, 2026 from 6 to 7:30 p.m. at the 8 Star Event Center.
claims.verbatim: The Department of the Air Force (DAF) invites community members to attend the August 2026 Microreactor Project Town Hall on August 26, from 6-7:30 p.m. at the 8 Star Event Center.
claims.source_outlet: 354th Fighter Wing Public Affairs, Eielson Air Force Base
claims.note: Primary source, inside the window.

claims.claim: The Eielson microreactor town hall is free and open to the public.
claims.verbatim: This event is free and open to the public.
claims.source_outlet: 354th Fighter Wing Public Affairs, Eielson Air Force Base
claims.note: The release also promises transparent, timely information and an open question and answer session.

claims.claim: The Eielson town hall release contains no megawatt figure, no mention of Oklo and no power purchase agreement term.
claims.verbatim: Megawatt Figure: Not mentioned
claims.source_outlet: 354th Fighter Wing Public Affairs, Eielson Air Force Base
claims.note: The 5 megawatt and 30 year figures come from a page that returned 503 and are DROPPED. They may not appear on a slide.

claims.claim: Public comment on ADL 234762 closes at 5:00 PM on Wednesday, August 19th, 2026.
claims.verbatim: Comment Period Ends 5:00PM, Wednesday, August 19, 2026
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Natural Resources, Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.note: Deduped off the deck, kept on the docket. The deadline is live and six days out.

claims.claim: The state proposes to convey approximately 19,950 acres in the Matanuska-Susitna Borough to the Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority.
claims.verbatim: proposes to convey approximately 19,950 acres (subject parcel) of State-owned land in the Matanuska-Susitna Borough to the Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority (AIDEA) through a noncompetitive public and charitable use conveyance
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Natural Resources, Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.note: The notice text does not itself mention AI or data centers, so that link must not be asserted from this document.
